items.author: BitcoinNewsCom
items.context: @BitcoinNewsCom (266.460 seguidores), en inglés: noticia fresca sobre Cypher Box, que lanzó un modo «Offline Seed-Signer» para convertir un Android viejo en firmante Bitcoin offline: dos teléfonos, comunicación solo por QR, semilla generada con dados, firma sin estado vía SeedQR, builds reproducibles y multisig con Sparrow y Nunchuk. Menciona el riesgo de privacidad de comprar una hardware wallet y los ataques a la cadena de suministro. Noticia de ~18 min con solo 2 respuestas (2.478 vistas). Calza directo con custodia air-gapped y con el incidente de generación de semillas de Coldcard de hoy.
items.suggested_text:
The dice part is the most underrated line here, and the timing makes it obvious why. Today's Coldcard postmortem traced 1,778.84 BTC stolen from over 8,600 addresses to a seed-generation flaw that security reviews missed for years. If the entropy is weak, every layer you add after it protects a key someone else can already rebuild.

An air-gapped signer with QR-only communication and a watch-only wallet online is the right architecture. It also flips the trust question: instead of trusting a vendor's chip and supply chain, you trust hardware you already own plus code and seeds you can verify yourself. Not zero trust, but trust you can audit.

I wrote up how to build that kind of setup from scratch: https://x.com/ForecastQuant/status/2123585216740528526

The harder part is rarely the device. It's what happens to the seed backup over the next ten years.
